name: Jan Hus
role: Priest, preacher at Bethlehem Chapel, rector of the University of Prague, reformer

died.place: Constance (Konstanz), burned at the stake by order of the Council of Constance

summary: Czech priest and university master who preached church reform in Prague, drawing on Wycliffe's ideas. Despite a promise of safe conduct, he was arrested at the Council of Constance and burned as a heretic, and his death set off the Hussite movement.

key_dates.label: Master of arts at the University of Prague
Becomes preacher at the Bethlehem Chapel, Prague
Elected rector of the University of Prague
Wycliffe's books burned in Prague; Hus excommunicated by the archbishop
Opposes the papal indulgence; leaves Prague for the countryside

accomplishments.text: Preached in Czech, not Latin, at the Bethlehem Chapel in Prague from 1402, drawing large crowds of ordinary people and calling for reform of clergy morals.
Served as rector of the University of Prague (1409–1410) after King Wenceslas IV gave the Czech masters control of the university.
Defended Wycliffe's writings in Prague when the church authorities ordered them surrendered and burned.
Publicly opposed the sale of indulgences to fund Pope John XXIII's war against King Ladislaus of Naples (1412).
Wrote The Church (De ecclesia, 1413), arguing that Christ, not the pope, is the head of the church, and that a pope or prelate who lives against Christ's law need not be obeyed.

Wrote extensively in Czech, including sermons and instruction for lay people, and is traditionally credited with reforming Czech spelling with diacritical marks (his authorship of that treatise is debated).
At the Council of Constance refused to recant unless shown from Scripture that he was wrong, and denied holding several of the views he was charged with.
Wrote letters from prison to friends in Bohemia that were preserved and widely read.

His execution sparked the Hussite movement and the Hussite Wars (1419–1434). The Unity of the Brethren, ancestor of the Moravian Church, grew out of his followers, and Luther wrote in 1520 that "we are all Hussites" without knowing it.

persecution_note: Hus was excommunicated several times, driven out of Prague, arrested at the Council of Constance in spite of the emperor-elect's safe-conduct, tried for heresy, and burned on 6 July 1415. There was no reigning pope when he was condemned. Pope John XXIII, under whom he was arrested, had fled Constance and been deposed, so the council itself passed judgment. In 1999 Pope John Paul II expressed "deep regret" for his cruel death.

persecution.title: Wycliffe's books burned; Hus excommunicated by the Archbishop of Prague
persecution.summary: The Archbishop of Prague ordered Wycliffe's writings surrendered. Using a bull of Pope Alexander V (December 1409) that banned preaching in private chapels such as the Bethlehem Chapel, he had about 200 Wycliffite manuscripts burned in July 1410 and excommunicated Hus for continuing to preach.

responsible.name: Zbyněk Zajíc of Hazmburk
responsible.role: Archbishop of Prague; burned the books and excommunicated Hus

responsible.name: Pope Alexander V
responsible.role: Issued the bull banning preaching in private chapels (Pisan line of popes during the Great Schism)

defended_by.name: King Wenceslas IV of Bohemia
defended_by.role: Supported Hus in these early years and opposed the archbishop

defended_by.name: Queen Sophia of Bavaria
defended_by.role: Queen of Bohemia; a patron of Hus

persecution.outcome: Hus kept preaching. The book burning caused riots in Prague.

persecution.title: Excommunicated by the papal court
persecution.summary: Hus was summoned to the papal court, but he sent representatives instead of going in person. Cardinal Odo Colonna, the judge in the case, excommunicated him for failing to appear.

responsible.name: Cardinal Odo Colonna
responsible.role: Judge in the curial case (later Pope Martin V)

responsible.name: Pope John XXIII
responsible.role: Pope (Pisan line) under whose authority the case was heard

persecution.outcome: He was excommunicated, but continued to preach with royal support.

persecution.title: Indulgence protest; protesters beheaded; interdict on Prague
persecution.summary: Pope John XXIII proclaimed indulgences to fund a crusade against King Ladislaus of Naples. Hus denounced them. Three young men who interrupted indulgence preachers were beheaded by the Prague city authorities. At the urging of Hus's opponents, including Michael de Causis, the curia renewed his excommunication and placed Prague under interdict, halting church services, for as long as he stayed in the city. King Wenceslas, wanting good relations with the pope, withdrew much of his support.

responsible.name: Pope John XXIII
responsible.role: Issued the indulgence; his curia aggravated the excommunication

responsible.name: Cardinal Peter degli Stefaneschi
responsible.role: Curial judge who pronounced the aggravated excommunication and interdict

responsible.name: Michael de Causis
responsible.role: Czech priest; pressed the case against Hus at the curia

responsible.name: Prague Old Town council
responsible.role: Executed the three young protesters
responsible.jurisdiction: Old Town of Prague, Kingdom of Bohemia

persecution.outcome: Hus left Prague in October 1412 and lived under noble protection in southern Bohemia until 1414.

persecution.title: Arrested at the Council of Constance despite a safe-conduct
persecution.summary: Hus went to the Council of Constance to defend himself under a safe-conduct from Sigismund, King of the Romans and later emperor. About three weeks after he arrived, he was summoned before the cardinals and arrested. He was held first in a Dominican friary on an island in the lake, then in the Bishop of Constance's castle at Gottlieben. Sigismund protested at first, but then accepted the council's position that its authority over heresy came before his promise.

responsible.name: Cardinals at the Council of Constance
responsible.role: Ordered the arrest
responsible.jurisdiction: Council of Constance, under Pope John XXIII

responsible.name: Pope John XXIII
responsible.role: Pope presiding over the council at the time of the arrest

responsible.name: Otto III of Hachberg
responsible.role: Bishop of Constance; held Hus in his castle at Gottlieben

responsible.name: Sigismund
responsible.role: King of the Romans; issued the safe-conduct, then let it be set aside

defended_by.name: John of Chlum
defended_by.role: Bohemian knight sent to protect Hus; publicly protested the arrest

defended_by.name: Wenceslas of Dubá
defended_by.role: Bohemian nobleman who accompanied and defended him

defended_by.name: Bohemian and Moravian nobles
defended_by.role: Sent formal protests to the council

persecution.outcome: He was imprisoned for over seven months, much of it in poor health.

persecution.title: Heresy trial and execution at Constance
persecution.summary: Hus was given public hearings on 5, 7, and 8 June 1415 before the council, with Cardinal Pierre d'Ailly prominent in the questioning. His accusers included Michael de Causis and his former friend Stephen Páleč, and the Paris theologian Jean Gerson pressed for his condemnation. He refused to recant articles he said he had never held, or to abjure others unless shown wrong from Scripture. On 6 July 1415 the council condemned him as a heretic in Constance Cathedral, and bishops ritually stripped him of his priesthood. He was handed to the secular power: Sigismund gave him to Louis III, Elector Palatine, who had him burned outside the city, and his ashes were thrown into the Rhine. There was no reigning pope at the time, since John XXIII had been deposed in May and Gregory XII had resigned on 4 July.

responsible.name: Council of Constance
responsible.role: Tried and condemned him
responsible.jurisdiction: General council of the Western Church

responsible.name: Cardinal Pierre d'Ailly
responsible.role: Leading questioner at the hearings

responsible.name: Jean Gerson
responsible.role: Chancellor of the University of Paris; pressed for condemnation
responsible.jurisdiction: University of Paris; Council of Constance

responsible.name: Stephen Páleč
responsible.role: Prague theologian, former friend; a principal accuser

responsible.name: Michael de Causis
responsible.role: A principal accuser

responsible.name: Sigismund
responsible.role: King of the Romans; handed him over for execution

responsible.name: Louis III, Elector Palatine
responsible.role: Carried out the sentence on Sigismund's order

responsible.name: City authorities of Constance
responsible.role: Executed him

persecution.outcome: Burned at the stake on 6 July 1415.

persecution.title: His companion Jerome of Prague burned
persecution.summary: Jerome of Prague, a scholar and Hus's ally who had come to Constance to support him, was arrested and pressured into a recantation, which he later withdrew. He was then condemned and burned at the same place as Hus.

responsible.name: Council of Constance
responsible.role: Condemned him as a relapsed heretic
responsible.jurisdiction: General council of the Western Church

persecution.outcome: Executed. News of both deaths turned Bohemia against the council and led to the Hussite revolt.
